exercises.prompt: What shows that a claim is an axiom, rather than a hypothesis you may set aside?

choices.text: Any attempt to deny it has to accept it and use it
It is true because it works for the person who asserts it
A majority has agreed to treat it as a starting rule
A revelation underwrites it, so no further question arises

feedback.note: An axiom is identified by the fact that its denial must use it, because the opponent has to rely on the very fact he is rejecting. Calling it a useful hypothesis treats a necessary starting point as an optional guess. A vote or a revelation would make the axiom depend on agreement or on mysticism, which a starting fact does not.

exercises.prompt: A speaker says, "Nothing exists," and offers that sentence as a discovery. What has the sentence already done?

choices.text: It has used existence: the denial is something he is asserting
It has shown that only ideas exist
It has shown that to be is to be perceived
It has taken a stand outside existence and checked from there

feedback.note: The sentence is something asserted, so the denial of existence already relies on there being a claim, because a speaker and a meaning are already in play. That is why the axiom wins. "Only ideas exist" and "to be is to be perceived" replace the something with a mind's contents. There is no stand outside existence from which the check could be made.

exercises.prompt: What does this passage establish about an attempt to deny an axiom?
exercises.quote: An axiom is a proposition that defeats its opponents by the fact that they have to accept it and use it in the process of any attempt to deny it.

choices.text: The opponent must accept the axiom and use it in the denial
The axiom wins because it is the most useful working rule
The axiom is a label one may drop without using any fact
The axiom holds only when a sacred source confirms it

feedback.quote: An axiom is a proposition that defeats its opponents by the fact that they have to accept it and use it in the process of any attempt to deny it.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 155
feedback.note: The passage says an axiom defeats its opponents because they have to accept it and use it in any attempt to deny it. Usefulness would make the test pragmatic, and a sacred source would make it mystical. A label one may drop leaves out the fact that the denial itself is already an instance of the axiom.

exercises.prompt: Which list names the first and primary axiomatic concepts, with identity in its proper relation to existence?

choices.text: Existence, identity as a corollary of existence, and consciousness
Wish, agreement, and a divine author of the world
Chance, constant conjunction, and a decree
A name for a philosophy, a slogan, and a political program

feedback.note: The primary axiomatic concepts are existence, identity, and consciousness, and identity is a corollary of existence because to be is already to be something. Wishes and decrees belong to the primacy-of-consciousness error. Chance and constant conjunction are rejected accounts of action. A name or a slogan is not a concept one must use in order to deny it.

exercises.prompt: Match each formula with the fact it names at the start.

feedback.note: Each formula names one of the three primary facts, because existence, identity, and consciousness are the start rather than three optional slogans. Something is; what is has a specific identity; awareness is awareness of that something. Swapping them would turn a corollary into a rival or would make awareness a substitute for the thing it perceives.

exercises.prompt: Someone demands a proof that existence exists which does not rely on existence at any step. What is the error?

choices.text: The demand asks for a proof that refuses the means any proof would use
Existence is a hypothesis kept only while it remains convenient
Only a divine mind can underwrite the fact that something is
Existence is real only for as long as it is perceived

feedback.note: A proof is something, offered by someone, with a specific meaning, so the demand for a proof that never uses existence rejects the only means a proof has. That is the axiomatic trap. Convenience would make the issue pragmatic, a divine underwriter would make it mystical, and "real only while perceived" denies the independence the axiom asserts.

exercises.prompt: Complete the account of why an axiom cannot be escaped by denying it.

parts.text: Any attempt to deny an axiom already requires

feedback.note: The denial has to use the axiom, because the attempt is itself an instance of existence, identity, or consciousness. Naming it, voting on it, or wishing it away treats the axiom as a label, a tally, or a feeling. None of those is what makes the denial fail. The denial fails because it relies on what it rejects.

exercises.prompt: Assemble the claim about how an axiom stands to its denial.

feedback.note: A denial must use the axiom it denies, because that use is what makes the axiom axiomatic. "Renames" would turn the point into a dispute about labels, and "escapes" would claim the very exit the axiom rules out. The order has to keep the denial as the thing that relies on the axiom, not as a route around it.

exercises.prompt: What does the axiom that existence exists claim?

choices.text: Something is, and it does not depend on being noticed
Only ideas exist
To be is to be perceived
Something is real only while a mind attends to it

feedback.note: Existence exists means that something is, independent of awareness, because a fact does not wait on a perceiver. "Only ideas exist" reduces what is to mental contents. "To be is to be perceived" makes existence a product of noticing. Both errors give consciousness the power the axiom denies it.

exercises.prompt: A rock lies in a canyon where no animal and no mind is present. Which conclusion follows?

choices.text: The rock exists, with no awareness of it required
The rock exists only as an idea in a mind that is absent
The rock waits to exist until some perceiver arrives
The canyon is there because someone wishes it to be

feedback.note: The rock is something, so it exists whether or not anyone is conscious of it. An idea in an absent mind is not a location for the rock, and waiting for a perceiver is the "to be is to be perceived" error. A wish does not hold a canyon in existence. Subjectivism and idealism both make the rock depend on a consciousness that is not there.

exercises.prompt: What does this passage establish about grasping that existence exists?
exercises.quote: Existence exists—and the act of grasping that statement implies two corollary axioms: that something exists which one perceives and that one exists possessing consciousness, consciousness being the faculty of perceiving that which exists.

choices.text: Something exists which one perceives, and one exists as conscious of it
Only the act of perceiving is real, and the object is optional
Consciousness can stand with no object and still be consciousness
What exists is whatever the perceiver decides the object is

feedback.quote: Existence exists—and the act of grasping that statement implies two corollary axioms: that something exists which one perceives and that one exists possessing consciousness, consciousness being the faculty of perceiving that which exists.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 124
feedback.note: Grasping the axiom implies two corollaries: something exists which one perceives, and the perceiver exists possessing consciousness, the faculty of perceiving that which exists. The object is not optional, because a consciousness with nothing to be conscious of is a contradiction. Letting the perceiver decide the object treats existence as a product of consciousness.

exercises.prompt: Why is a consciousness with nothing to be conscious of impossible?

choices.text: Awareness with no object cancels the idea of awareness
Only ideas exist, so an object would be an extra
To be is to be perceived, so an empty mind is the basic fact
A wish can stand in for the missing object

feedback.note: Consciousness is consciousness of something, so awareness of nothing is a contradiction in terms, because the idea of awareness cancels itself without an object. The idealist alternatives make the object unnecessary or make the empty mind the basic fact, which reverses the axiom. A wish is not an object. The contradiction does not describe a world that exists unseen.

exercises.prompt: Match each claim with the view it expresses.

pairs.left: To be is to be perceived
pairs.right: Existence made to depend on a mind

pairs.left: A wish is enough to make it so

feedback.note: The axiom says something is, whether or not it is noticed, because existence does not depend on awareness. Idealism leaves only ideas. "To be is to be perceived" ties being to a mind. Subjectivism puts a wish in the place of a fact. Each rival denies the independence the axiom asserts, and none of them is a restatement of it.

exercises.prompt: A theory says the world is the set of ideas, and that an unperceived thing is nothing. Which error is this?

choices.text: It replaces what exists with the contents of a mind
It treats a change over time as a contradiction
It says a thing can act against its nature
It confuses a built structure with a mountain

feedback.note: Calling the world a set of ideas, and unperceived things nothing, is idealism: it denies that something exists independent of awareness. Change over time, action against a nature, and the difference between a building and a mountain are other issues. They do not name this error. This error is the reduction of existence to mental contents.

exercises.prompt: Complete the axiom as a claim about what is, apart from awareness.

parts.text: is, apart from any awareness of it.

feedback.note: The axiom says that something is, because existence is not a blank and not a mental product. "Nothing" is nonexistence, not a substitute for what is. A wish or a vote would make the fact depend on a feeling or a tally, which is subjectivism. Awareness can grasp the something; it does not have to be present for the something to be.

exercises.prompt: Assemble the claim that something is, apart from awareness.

feedback.note: Something exists independent of awareness, because the axiom is about what is, not about what a mind contains. Inserting "ideas" or "wishes" would make existence depend on consciousness, which is the idealist or subjectivist reversal. The claim stays intact only when independence from awareness is what is asserted.

exercises.prompt: What does it mean to exist, once identity is stated?

choices.text: To be something of a specific nature
To be nothing in particular
To be whatever a viewer feels it to be
To be barred from ever acting

feedback.note: To exist is to be something of a specific nature, because identity is a corollary of existence: a something with no nature would be a nothing. A feeling does not assign the nature, which is the subjectivist error. Identity does not forbid action. It says that whatever the thing does, it does as the kind of thing it is.

exercises.prompt: A leaf is green in summer and red in autumn. It is never both colors all over at once. What does identity say?

choices.text: The change across time is not a contradiction
The leaf was both colors in the same respect at the same time
Identity forbids the leaf to change color at all
The autumn color rewrites the fact that it was green

feedback.note: A contradiction would be the same leaf all red and all green in the same respect at the same time. Green, then red, is change, and change is not a contradiction. Forbidding the change treats identity as a ban on action. Rewriting the past treats a later state as if it could erase an earlier fact, which identity does not allow either.

exercises.prompt: What does this passage establish about a contradiction?
exercises.quote: To arrive at a contradiction is to confess an error in one's thinking; to maintain a contradiction is to abdicate one's mind and to evict oneself from the realm of reality.

choices.text: It confesses an error in thinking; keeping it abandons reality
It reports a feature of reality that thought must accept
It is a deeper fact than identity and outranks A is A
It is the name for ordinary change across time

feedback.quote: To arrive at a contradiction is to confess an error in one's thinking; to maintain a contradiction is to abdicate one's mind and to evict oneself from the realm of reality.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 125
feedback.note: Arriving at a contradiction confesses an error in one's thinking, and maintaining it abdicates the mind, because reality does not contain the clash. Treating the clash as a feature of reality inverts that confession. Change over time is not the contradiction this passage names. A contradiction does not outrank identity; it shows that the thinking failed to respect identity.

exercises.prompt: Someone says, "A is A, so nothing can act." What is wrong with that inference?

choices.text: Identity keeps a thing to its nature; action that fits the nature is not a breach
A is A is only a custom about how words are used
Action is real only when it breaks identity
A thing is whatever it later becomes, and it has no nature in the meantime

feedback.note: A is A does not mean stillness. A thing acts as the thing it is, so action that fits its nature is identity applied, not a breach. Calling the law a verbal custom drops the fact. Requiring action to break identity makes a contradiction the condition of doing anything. A thing with no nature until later is not yet anything.

exercises.prompt: Match each case with the fact, or the error, it actually is.

pairs.left: All red and all green at once
A thing acts as the kind of thing it is
Calling the clash a fact of the world

feedback.note: The same clash at the same time and in the same respect is a contradiction, and it is an error in thinking rather than a feature of the world. A later state is change, not that clash. Action that fits what the thing is does not break A is A. Mixing these up either freezes the world or pretends reality contradicts itself.

exercises.prompt: A clerk says the same bill is both paid and unpaid, in the same respect, at the same time, and that the world contains the clash. What is the right verdict?

choices.text: The clash is in the record of the thinking; the bill is not both
Identity allows both if the clerk feels strongly enough
A vote of the office can make both descriptions true together
One event following another makes both the cause

feedback.note: Paid and unpaid in the same respect at once is a contradiction, so it confesses an error in the clerk's thinking rather than a fact about the bill. A feeling or a vote would be subjectivism, letting preference rewrite identity. Constant conjunction does not cause a thing to be both itself and its opposite. The bill is one or the other in that respect.

exercises.prompt: Complete the statement of what identity adds to the bare word "exist."

parts.text: To exist is to be something of

feedback.note: To exist is to be something of a specific nature, because a nature-free something would not be distinguishable from nothing. "No nature" drops identity. A wish or a vote would make the nature depend on feeling or agreement, which is subjectivism. The nature is what the thing is, not a label added after the fact.

exercises.prompt: Assemble the claim about where a contradiction is located.

feedback.note: A contradiction is an error in thinking, because reality is not both of two opposites in the same respect at once. "A feature of reality" is the tempting misplacement: it treats the mind's clash as a discovery about the world. That mistake gives up identity. Change over time is a different fact and is not what this claim calls a contradiction.

exercises.prompt: What does consciousness do with what exists?

choices.text: It perceives and identifies what exists; it does not create it
It creates the objects it then seems to find
It is aware of nothing but itself
It turns wishes into the things it names

feedback.note: Consciousness is the faculty of perceiving that which exists, and its work is identification, not creation. A consciousness conscious only of itself is a contradiction, because awareness needs an object. Turning wishes into things is a caricature, not the claim at issue, and it is also false. The mind does not decree the existence it perceives.

exercises.prompt: An astronomer identifies a planet that was already on its course before anyone knew of it. What happened?

choices.text: Consciousness identified an existent; it did not bring the planet into being
The identification created the planet
The planet exists only as a form of the astronomer's intuition
The wish to find a planet was the planet

feedback.note: The planet existed, and the astronomer perceived and identified it. Identification does not create its object. Treating the planet as a form of intuition is the Kantian claim that we do not know things as they are, apart from the mind's structuring. A wish is not an object. Subjectivism and the primacy of consciousness both erase the planet that was already there.

exercises.prompt: What does this passage establish about the faculty of consciousness?
exercises.quote: Consciousness is the faculty of awareness—the faculty of perceiving that which exists.

choices.text: Consciousness perceives that which exists
Consciousness writes the existence it then perceives
Consciousness is a feeling that needs no object
Consciousness perceives only its own forms, never things

feedback.quote: Consciousness is the faculty of awareness—the faculty of perceiving that which exists.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, "Concepts of Consciousness," Introduction to Objectivist Epistemology, 37
feedback.note: The passage names consciousness as the faculty of awareness, the faculty of perceiving that which exists. It does not say that consciousness creates its object. A feeling with no object would be a consciousness of nothing, which is a contradiction. "Only its own forms" is Kant's primacy-of-consciousness claim, and this passage does not teach it. Perception here is of what exists.

exercises.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Kant's forms of intuition?

choices.text: The mind's forms structure experience, so we do not know things as they are
Wishes are rocks, and rocks are wishes
The senses invent their objects by taking a vote
Things act against their natures whenever a mind is present

feedback.note: Kant's forms of intuition mean that space and time, as the mind's forms, structure experience, so we do not know things as they are apart from that structuring. That is a primacy-of-consciousness claim. It is not the claim that wishes are rocks. A vote does not invent sensory objects, and the forms are not a theory of action against identity. The error is epistemic and metaphysical: the mind's structuring replaces things as they are.

exercises.prompt: Match each item with the role it has in this account of consciousness.

pairs.left: Forms that hide things as they are

feedback.note: Consciousness perceives and identifies what exists; it does not create it. Kant's forms are a primacy-of-consciousness claim because they deny knowledge of things as they are, not because they turn wishes into rocks. Awareness with no object cancels itself. Confusing these roles either makes the mind a legislator of existence or pretends an empty consciousness is possible.

exercises.prompt: A philosopher says, "I am conscious only of my consciousness, never of a thing that exists apart from it." What is the verdict?

choices.text: A consciousness conscious only of itself is a contradiction
This is the axiom that existence exists
This shows that identity forbids every action
This is a man-made fact one must accept without judgment

feedback.note: Awareness is awareness of something that exists, so a consciousness conscious of nothing but itself is a contradiction in terms, because it withholds the object. The view does not state the axiom of existence. Identity and action are not the issue, and the claim is not a man-made fact to be filed and accepted. The error is an objectless, self-only consciousness.

exercises.prompt: Complete the formula that states what consciousness does.

parts.text: , not the creating of its object.

feedback.note: Consciousness is identification, because it perceives and identifies what exists rather than bringing it into being. "Creation" reverses the faculty and makes the object a mental product. A wish or a vote would make the object depend on feeling or agreement, which is subjectivism. What exists has a nature, and consciousness identifies it.

exercises.prompt: Assemble the claim about what consciousness perceives.

feedback.note: Consciousness perceives that which exists, because its faculty is awareness of something, not a power to bring that something into being. "Creates" or "decrees" would turn the faculty into a primacy-of-consciousness claim. The mind identifies the existent. It does not legislate it, and a consciousness of nothing is not a third option this claim allows.

exercises.prompt: How do "Existence exists," "Consciousness is conscious," and "A is A" stand to one another?

choices.text: As one set: something is, it is what it is, and awareness grasps it
As three rival theories, of which one may be kept and the others dropped
As optional names for a single mood
As decrees a mind may rewrite if they become inconvenient

feedback.note: The three formulas are one set, because each names a fact the others already rely on. Dropping one as a rival pretends you can keep existence while discarding what it is, or keep awareness while discarding its object. A mood is subjectivism. A decree that rewrites them is primacy of consciousness. None of the three is optional.

exercises.prompt: What does this passage establish about existence and about consciousness?
exercises.quote: Existence is Identity, Consciousness is Identification.

choices.text: What exists has identity, and consciousness identifies it
Consciousness creates the identity it then reports
Identity and consciousness are one and the same faculty
Identification replaces existence and makes the object unnecessary

feedback.quote: Existence is Identity, Consciousness is Identification.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 124
feedback.note: Existence is identity: to be is to be something. Consciousness is identification: it grasps that something. Consciousness does not create identity, and it is not itself the law of identity. Identification without an existent would be awareness of nothing, which is a contradiction. The passage ties the three axioms into one statement.

exercises.prompt: Why is identity not a second start, laid beside existence and free to contradict it?

choices.text: Identity is a corollary: to exist is already to be something
Identity is a man-made rule added later by agreement
Identity applies only while nothing acts
Identity is the product of a divine consciousness

feedback.note: Identity is a corollary of existence, because something with no specific nature would not be something. A later agreement would make identity man-made and optional. Restricting it to stillness confuses identity with a ban on action. A divine author of identity is primacy of consciousness. The corollary cannot be set against the axiom it follows from.

exercises.prompt: Once the three axioms are granted, why is the primacy of existence the next question?

choices.text: Consciousness is real, so one must say whether it apprehends existence or claims to produce it
Primacy means a wish outranks the fact it is about
The axioms already say that the universe is a product of consciousness
Primacy cancels identity and leaves existence without a nature

feedback.note: The axioms include consciousness as well as existence, so the next question is which is primary. Primacy of existence says consciousness apprehends what exists and does not produce it. A wish outranking a fact is subjectivism. The axioms do not say the universe is a mental product; that reversal is what primacy of existence rejects. Primacy does not cancel identity.

exercises.prompt: Match each denial with the fact the denial itself uses.

pairs.left: The claim that a thing is not what it is
pairs.right: The claim still has one specific meaning

pairs.left: The claim that no one is conscious
pairs.right: The claim is an act of awareness

pairs.left: The claim that action breaks identity
pairs.right: Identity is being used, then set aside

feedback.note: Each denial uses the axiom it rejects, because that is what makes the three formulas one set. "Nothing exists" is asserted as something. A denial of identity still means one specific thing. A denial of consciousness is conscious. Setting action outside identity uses identity and then pretends action is exempt. The set leaves no such exemption.

exercises.prompt: A thinker accepts that something exists, then says consciousness assigns what each thing is. Which axiom has he kept in words and dropped in practice?

choices.text: Identity: he lets a mind decide the nature instead of identifying it
None: assigning natures is what "consciousness is conscious" means
Existence: he has denied that anything is
He has only restated that change over time is allowed

feedback.note: If consciousness assigns what things are, identity is no longer a corollary of existence; it has become a mental product. That is primacy of consciousness, not "consciousness is conscious." He has not denied that something is, but he has denied that it is what it is independent of the mind. Change over time is a different issue and does not license assigned natures.

exercises.prompt: Complete the relation of identity to existence.

parts.text: of existence, not a rival start.

feedback.note: Identity is a corollary of existence because to exist is already to be something of a specific nature. A rival start would let identity contradict existence. A product or a wish would make the nature depend on a consciousness, which reverses primacy. The three formulas stay one set only when identity is that corollary and consciousness identifies rather than assigns.

exercises.prompt: Assemble the paired formula that keeps existence, identity, and consciousness together.

feedback.note: Existence is identity, and consciousness is identification, because what is has a nature and consciousness grasps that nature. "Creates" would make consciousness the author of identity. "Replaces" would drop the existent in favor of the act of identifying it. Either word breaks the set. The formula does not say that consciousness and identity are the same fact.

exercises.prompt: What does the primacy of existence say about the universe?

choices.text: It exists independent of any consciousness, and it has a specific identity
It exists only while some mind perceives it
It is the product of a divine consciousness
It has no nature until a human mind assigns one

feedback.note: The primacy of existence says the universe exists independent of any consciousness, human or divine, and that things are what they are. "Only while perceived" is the claim that to be is to be perceived. A divine author, or a human assignment of natures, makes the universe a product of consciousness. Independence includes a specific identity; it does not mean a blank.

exercises.prompt: Suppose no human being and no god were aware of a certain star. What follows?

choices.text: The star would still exist, and it would still be what it is
The star would lapse, because to be is to be perceived
The star would remain only as an idea, with no universe left
A wish could keep the star in existence in their absence

feedback.note: The star exists independent of any consciousness, so the absence of a human or divine mind does not remove it or its identity. "To be is to be perceived" is the rival claim. Leaving only an idea is idealism. A wish cannot hold a star in existence, because a feeling is not a substitute for the fact. The case applies the axiom to a world with no observer.

exercises.prompt: What does this passage establish about existence and consciousness?
exercises.quote: The primacy of existence (of reality) is the axiom that existence exists, i.e., that the universe exists independent of consciousness (of any consciousness), that things are what they are, that they possess a specific nature, an identity.

choices.text: The universe exists independent of any consciousness, and things have identity
The universe is the product of a consciousness
Independence means the universe has no specific nature
A divine consciousness is the one mind the axiom still allows as author

feedback.quote: The primacy of existence (of reality) is the axiom that existence exists, i.e., that the universe exists independent of consciousness (of any consciousness), that things are what they are, that they possess a specific nature, an identity.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, "The Metaphysical Versus the Man-Made," Philosophy: Who Needs It, 24
feedback.note: The passage states the primacy of existence: the universe exists independent of consciousness, of any consciousness, and things possess a specific nature, an identity. A product of consciousness is the reversal the next claim names, not this one. Independence does not drop identity. "Any consciousness" leaves no divine exception, because a god's mind is still a consciousness.

exercises.prompt: The phrase "independent of any consciousness" excludes which authors of the universe?

choices.text: Both human consciousness and divine consciousness
Human minds only, leaving a god as the author of existence
Divine minds only, leaving human agreement as the author
Neither, whenever the feeling of independence is strong

feedback.note: The axiom says independent of any consciousness, so neither a human mind nor a divine mind is the author of the universe. A divine exception is still primacy of consciousness. Human agreement as author is the same reversal in a secular form, and it is subjectivism when the agreement is a feeling. Strength of feeling does not create an exception the axiom forbids.

exercises.prompt: Match each claim with the view it expresses.

pairs.left: The universe exists with no mind required
The universe is a mind's product
To be is to be perceived

feedback.note: Primacy of existence keeps the universe independent of every consciousness and keeps its identity, because things are what they are whether or not they are known. Primacy of consciousness makes the universe a product of a mind. "To be is to be perceived" denies independence directly. Identity is part of the primacy of existence, not a third theory beside it.

exercises.prompt: Someone says the universe exists only because a god thought it into being. Which claim is that?

choices.text: Primacy of consciousness: a mind, here divine, is the author of the universe
Primacy of existence, because a god is not a human being
Nothing but a restatement that A is A
The classification of the universe as a man-made fact

feedback.note: A universe thought into being by a god is a product of a consciousness, so the claim is primacy of consciousness. A divine mind does not become an exemption, because the axiom says any consciousness. The claim does not restate identity; it sets a will above identity. The universe is not a man-made fact, because man-made facts are products of human choice inside a universe that already exists.

exercises.prompt: Complete the independence claim so that no mind, human or divine, is left as author.

parts.text: The universe exists independent of any

feedback.note: The universe exists independent of any consciousness, because primacy of existence rules out every mind as author, human or divine. A wish or a vote would name a particular human attitude, and chance would name a different rejected ruler of nature. The word that closes the exemption is consciousness. Identity remains: what exists is still something specific.

exercises.prompt: Assemble the independence claim, including identity.

feedback.note: The universe exists independent of consciousness, with identity, because primacy of existence includes both independence and a specific nature. "By decree" would make a will the author and would state the primacy of consciousness instead. The order has to keep existence first and identity as what that existence has, not as an optional addition a mind may withhold.

exercises.prompt: Once existence is primary, what is the work of consciousness?

choices.text: It apprehends what exists; it does not create what it apprehends
It produces the objects it then seems to discover
It perceives only its own structure, never things
It replaces the identity of things with a feeling

feedback.note: Consciousness apprehends what exists; it does not create it, because the universe is already there with a specific identity. Producing the objects is primacy of consciousness. Perceiving only the mind's structure is Kant's claim that we do not know things as they are. A feeling in place of identity is subjectivism. Apprehension takes the existent as it is.

exercises.prompt: You open your eyes and see a river. Which order is the right one?

choices.text: The river exists, and seeing takes it in
Seeing brings the river into existence
The forms of intuition are the river
The wish to see water is the river

feedback.note: The river exists independent of the seeing, and consciousness apprehends it, because perception does not create its object. "Seeing brings it into existence" is "to be is to be perceived." Equating the river with the forms of intuition is Kant's primacy of consciousness, not a description of apprehension. A wish is not a river. The order is existence first, awareness second.

exercises.prompt: What does this passage establish about awareness?
exercises.quote: Awareness is awareness of something.

choices.text: Awareness takes an object that is something; it is not awareness of nothing
The something is created by the act of awareness
Awareness of something means that only ideas exist
The something is a mental form that hides the thing as it is

feedback.quote: Awareness is awareness of something.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, "Concepts of Consciousness," Introduction to Objectivist Epistemology, 37
feedback.note: The passage establishes that awareness is of something, so a consciousness with nothing to be conscious of is not awareness. It does not say the act creates the something. "Only ideas exist" would drop the object into the mind. A form that hides the thing is Kant's claim, and this sentence does not teach it. The object is something that is.

exercises.prompt: Kant holds that we know things only as the mind's forms structure them. How does the primacy of existence answer?

choices.text: That story makes the object a mental product and gives up things as they are
It agrees, and adds that the forms are wishes
It says the forms are settled by a vote of observers
It says identity forbids consciousness to perceive at all

feedback.note: Kant's forms of intuition mean we do not know things as they are, apart from the mind's structuring, and that is a primacy-of-consciousness claim, because the object we are allowed is structured by mind. The answer is not that wishes are the forms, and it is not a vote. Identity does not forbid perception. Apprehension is perception of things as they are, not of a substitute the mind builds.

exercises.prompt: Match each description with the act or error it names.

pairs.left: Taking in a fact that was already there
Treating the fact as the mind's product
pairs.right: Creation, which consciousness does not do

pairs.left: Structuring experience so things as they are stay unknown
Letting a feeling stand in for the fact

feedback.note: Apprehension takes in what already exists, because consciousness does not create its object. Treating the fact as a mental product is the creation error. Kant's forms leave things as they are unknown, which is primacy of consciousness, not the claim that wishes are things. A feeling in place of the fact is subjectivism. Each rival drops the object that apprehension requires.

exercises.prompt: Someone says, "If no one has conceived a law of nature, the law is not there." What is the error?

choices.text: Failing to conceive a fact does not remove the fact; conception identifies it
An unconceived law is man-made, because no one has chosen it yet
Conception creates the way entities act
An unconceived regularity is a contradiction in nature

feedback.note: A law of nature, as the identity of the entities that act, is there to be apprehended, because failure to conceive it does not erase it. Calling it man-made confuses a natural fact with a product of choice. Conception does not create the action of entities. An unknown fact is not a contradiction; a contradiction would be an error in the thinking that denies the fact.

exercises.prompt: Complete the statement of what consciousness does with reality.

feedback.note: Consciousness apprehends reality, because the universe exists independent of it and consciousness takes that universe in. "Create," "decree," and "replace" each state the primacy of consciousness in a different wording. None of them is the work of a faculty whose object is something that already is. Apprehension identifies; it does not legislate.

exercises.prompt: Assemble the claim that consciousness takes reality in and does not produce it.

feedback.note: Consciousness apprehends reality and does not create it, because primacy of existence leaves the object independent of the mind. "Wishes" or "decrees" would put a feeling or a will in the place of apprehension. The claim is not that consciousness is passive in the sense of being unable to identify. It identifies what is. It does not bring it into being.

exercises.prompt: Which of these can rewrite a fact that already is?

choices.text: None of a wish, a belief, or an agreement can rewrite it
A wish cannot, but a formal agreement can rewrite a natural fact
All three can, because consciousness decrees the facts
A measurement can, because a number is a kind of feeling

feedback.note: A wish, a belief, and an agreement leave the fact as it is, because facts are independent of feelings, wishes, hopes, and fears. Granting the power to an agreement is still primacy of consciousness, only in a collective form. A measurement apprehends a quantity; it does not decree one, and a number is not a feeling. No mental act rewrites what is.

exercises.prompt: Observers agree that an eclipse will not occur. It occurs on the predicted course. What does the agreement change?

choices.text: Nothing about the eclipse; the agreement is not a decree over the fact
The eclipse, which becomes unreal once the agreement is sincere
The fact, but only if the agreement counts as a perception
The orbits, because to be is to be agreed upon

feedback.note: The eclipse occurs because the entities act as they are, and agreement does not decree a change. Sincerity is a fact about the observers, not a cause in the sky. Treating agreement as perception confuses apprehension with creation. "To be is to be agreed upon" is a social version of "to be is to be perceived." The fact stands.

exercises.prompt: What does this passage establish about facts and about feelings?
exercises.quote: Reality exists as an objective absolute—facts are facts, independent of man's feelings, wishes, hopes or fears.

choices.text: Facts are facts, independent of feelings, wishes, hopes, or fears
Feelings are the test of which facts exist
A hope can annul a fact the hoper rejects
Facts are absolute only when everyone agrees to them

feedback.quote: Reality exists as an objective absolute—facts are facts, independent of man's feelings, wishes, hopes or fears.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, "Introducing Objectivism," The Objectivist Newsletter, August 1962, 35
feedback.note: The passage says reality exists as an objective absolute: facts are facts, independent of man's feelings, wishes, hopes, or fears. Feelings are not a test of existence, and a hope does not annul what it rejects, because that would make consciousness a decree. Universal agreement is still a state of consciousness. The absolute does not wait on it.

exercises.prompt: What does "Nature, to be commanded, must be obeyed" claim?

choices.text: You succeed only by treating things as what they are
A decree can order nature to drop its identity
Obedience means accepting whatever people wish were so
Command is a mental act that creates the result it names

feedback.note: To command nature one must obey it, because action works only when it respects identity. A decree that drops identity is primacy of consciousness. Obedience to a wish is subjectivism. Command does not create the result; it uses what the entities already are. The line rejects the idea that will can rewrite the fact it wants to use.

exercises.prompt: Match each item with what it can, or cannot, do to a fact.

pairs.right: Stands whether or not anyone agrees

feedback.note: A wish and an agreement cannot rewrite a fact, because facts are independent of consciousness. The fact stands without the agreement. A decree of will is the picture primacy of existence rejects: nature is not ruled by will. Treating any of those mental acts as a cause confuses apprehension, or mere wanting, with a power to legislate existence.

exercises.prompt: A navigator calls a shoal unreal because the shorter course works better on the chart. The ship then strikes the shoal. Which error was the chart?

choices.text: Pragmatism: treating a convenient claim as if convenience could change the shoal
A correct decree, because a working plan outranks a reef
Identity applied to action, because the shorter course was an action
Apprehension, because the chart took the shoal in as it was

feedback.note: The chart was pragmatic: it treated truth as what works, and a convenient blank does not move a shoal, because the fact is not a tool of convenience. A working plan is not a decree over rock and water. The shorter course was an action that ignored identity, not an application of it. Apprehension would have kept the shoal on the chart. The wreck follows from the entities, not from the wish.

exercises.prompt: Complete the line that rejects commanding nature by decree.

parts.text: Nature, to be commanded, must be

feedback.note: Nature must be obeyed, because you can use a thing only by treating it as what it is. Wishing, voting, or fearing leaves the thing unchanged and does not constitute command. Those alternatives are subjectivism or primacy of consciousness. Obedience here is respect for identity, not submission to someone else's feeling.

exercises.prompt: Assemble the claim that facts do not depend on wishes.

feedback.note: Facts are independent of wishes, because a feeling does not rewrite what exists. "Created by decree" would state the opposite, the primacy of consciousness. The claim does not say facts are independent of the entities that constitute them. It says they are independent of the mental acts that would like them to be otherwise.

exercises.prompt: What does the primacy of consciousness claim about the universe?

choices.text: The claim that the universe is the product of a consciousness, human or divine or both
The claim that the universe exists whether or not any mind is aware of it
The claim that a thing cannot act against its nature
The claim that man-made facts must be judged rather than worshipped

feedback.note: The primacy of consciousness claims that the universe has no independent existence and is the product of a consciousness, human or divine or both, because that is the reversal of the axioms. The independent universe is the primacy of existence. Action according to nature is causality, and judging man-made facts is a later distinction. Neither of those is the reversal the definition names.

exercises.prompt: Which pair is the real opposition between the two primacies?

choices.text: The universe exists on its own, versus the universe is a mind's product
Wishes are rocks, versus rocks are wishes
Change over time, versus action that fits a nature
A mountain, versus a building someone raised

feedback.note: The opposition is independent existence versus a universe produced by consciousness, because that is the reversal of the axioms. "Wishes are rocks" is a caricature, not Kant's claim and not the definition of either primacy. Change versus action is an identity issue. A mountain and a building differ as given and man-made, which presupposes that both exist and does not decide which primacy is true.

exercises.prompt: What does this passage establish about rejecting the axioms of existence?
exercises.quote: The rejection of these axioms represents a reversal: the primacy of consciousness—the notion that the universe has no independent existence, that it is the product of a consciousness (either human or divine or both).

choices.text: The rejection reverses them into the claim that a consciousness produces the universe
The reversal means that things keep a specific nature and nothing more is changed
The reversal leaves the universe independent and adds only a human mood
A divine consciousness is exempt and does not count as the product-claim

feedback.quote: The rejection of these axioms represents a reversal: the primacy of consciousness—the notion that the universe has no independent existence, that it is the product of a consciousness (either human or divine or both).
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, "The Metaphysical Versus the Man-Made," Philosophy: Who Needs It, 24
feedback.note: Rejecting the axioms is a reversal: the primacy of consciousness, the notion that the universe has no independent existence and is the product of a consciousness, either human or divine or both. The reversal does not preserve independence or identity. A mood is too weak a name for a claim about the author of the universe. Divine consciousness is included, not exempt.

exercises.prompt: Someone says a created universe is still the primacy of existence, because the creator is a god and not a human being. What is wrong?

choices.text: The axiom rules out any consciousness, divine included, as the author of the universe
Primacy of existence allows a divine exception and forbids only human wishes
Only human feelings are barred; a sacred decree is just another fact
Kant's forms are the same claim as a god's wish becoming a rock

feedback.note: A god's mind is a consciousness, so a universe it creates is still a product of consciousness, because the primacy of existence says independent of any consciousness. There is no divine exception. A sacred decree is mysticism, not a neutral fact. Kant's forms are a different primacy-of-consciousness claim, about the mind's structuring, and they are not the claim that wishes are rocks.

exercises.prompt: Match each formula with the primacy it states.

pairs.left: The universe is independent of any consciousness
The universe is the product of a consciousness

feedback.note: Primacy of existence keeps the universe independent and identical, because things are what they are apart from any mind. Primacy of consciousness makes the universe a product of a mind, and the mind may be human, divine, or both. Leaving the divine case out would fake an exemption. Identity belongs on the existence side; the reversal gives the universe no independent nature.

exercises.prompt: A skeptic says we cannot know things as they are, only as our forms deliver them. Which metaphysical claim is doing the work?

choices.text: Primacy of consciousness: the object we may claim is structured by mind
Primacy of existence: the forms simply are the things as they are
Causality read as constant conjunction and nothing more
The rule that a metaphysically given fact is settled by a vote

feedback.note: If we cannot know things as they are, apart from the mind's forms, the object has been given over to consciousness, because that is Kant's primacy-of-consciousness claim. It does not say the forms are the things. Constant conjunction is a theory of causation, and a vote is not what the forms are. The skeptic here is not neutral. He has reversed which side is primary.

exercises.prompt: Complete the definition of the primacy of consciousness.

feedback.note: The universe, on this reversal, is the product of a consciousness, because it is denied any independent existence. "Identity" and "corollary" belong to the primacy of existence, where things are what they are. "Standard" belongs to a later question about value. The word that marks the reversal is product, and the consciousness may be human or divine or both.

exercises.prompt: Assemble the rejection of a mind-made universe.

feedback.note: The universe is not a mind's product, because primacy of existence denies that any consciousness, human or divine, authors it. "Wish" and "decree" name the kind of mental cause the reversal relies on, and inserting them would state that error or blur it. The claim to assemble is the rejection: independent existence, with identity, and no mental author.

exercises.prompt: Which set states the three lines at once: independence, apprehension, and no decree?

choices.text: The universe exists apart from minds, minds take it in, and no wish rewrites it
The universe is a mind's product, seeing creates it, and a vote can revise it
Existence depends on perception, identity is optional, and will rules nature
Facts are man-made, seeing is a chosen percept, and chance rules action

feedback.note: The three lines are one claim, because independence, apprehension, and the refusal of decree all follow from the primacy of existence. The second set is the primacy of consciousness. The third makes being depend on perception and hands nature to will. The fourth confuses the given with the man-made and treats chance as a ruler. Only the first set holds all three lines.

exercises.prompt: What does this passage establish about what rules nature?
exercises.quote: Whether its basic constituent elements are atoms, or subatomic particles, or some yet undiscovered forms of energy, it is not ruled by a consciousness or by will or by chance, but by the Law of Identity.

choices.text: Nature is ruled by the Law of Identity, not by a consciousness, a will, or chance
The basic elements are whichever kind a mind prefers to posit
Chance is one form of the Law of Identity
A will may rule nature in any region identity leaves open

feedback.quote: Whether its basic constituent elements are atoms, or subatomic particles, or some yet undiscovered forms of energy, it is not ruled by a consciousness or by will or by chance, but by the Law of Identity.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, "The Metaphysical Versus the Man-Made," Philosophy: Who Needs It, 25
feedback.note: Whatever the constituents are, nature is not ruled by a consciousness or by will or by chance, but by the Law of Identity, because that is what primacy forbids a decree to do. Preference about the elements does not decide them. Chance is not a species of identity. There is no region identity leaves open for a will, because identity is the ruler, not a temporary default.

exercises.prompt: A thinker grants that the universe is independent of minds, then adds that a prayer can suspend a natural law for a day. What has he dropped?

choices.text: The refusal of decree: a will does not suspend identity
Nothing: a one-day suspension is only change over time
Apprehension, which he applied correctly by praying
Independence, which means a will may edit identity

feedback.note: A prayer that suspends a law is a decree of will over nature, so he has kept a verbal independence and dropped the refusal of decree, because identity, not will, rules action. The suspension is not ordinary change; change is an entity acting as what it is, not a will switching off that nature. Prayer is not apprehension. Independence does not license editing.

exercises.prompt: Another thinker says wishes do not rewrite facts, then adds that the facts we can know are only our forms. What has he kept, and what has he lost?

choices.text: He has kept the refusal of whim and lost independence, because the object is now mental
He has stated all three lines, since forms are how apprehension works
He has lost nothing: Kant's forms are things as they are
He has reduced the issue to the difference between a building and a mountain

feedback.note: Refusing the power of a wish is only one line. If the knowable object is a form the mind supplies, independence is gone, because we no longer claim things as they are. That is Kant's primacy of consciousness, not apprehension. The forms are not the things. A building and a mountain are both existents inside an independent universe; they do not settle this reversal.

exercises.prompt: Match each part of the coastline case with the line it illustrates.

pairs.left: The coast was there before anyone measured it
The measurement takes the coast as it is
Wanting a harbor leaves the rock where it is
Calling the rock a product of the survey

feedback.note: The coast exists before the survey, the survey apprehends it, and the wish for a harbor does not move it, because those are the three lines together. Calling the rock a product of the survey reverses primacy: it makes consciousness the author of the object. A measurement is not a decree, and a wish is not a cause in the rock.

exercises.prompt: You measure a coast that exists whether or not you measure it, and your wish for a harbor does not move the rock. Which lines are present?

choices.text: Independent existence, apprehension by the measurement, and no decree by the wish
The rock is man-made, because a person measured it
The wish is a metaphysically given fact about the rock
The measurement creates the coast it reports

feedback.note: All three lines are in the case, because the coast does not depend on the measurer, the measurement takes it in, and the wish does not rewrite it. Measuring does not make the rock man-made. A wish is not a given fact about the rock; the rock is. Creation by measurement is the primacy of consciousness, which the case does not illustrate.

exercises.prompt: Complete the statement of what rules nature.

parts.text: Nature is ruled by the law of

feedback.note: Nature is ruled by the law of identity, because what exists has a specific nature and acts as that nature. Chance, will, and decree are the rulers the primacy of existence rejects. Putting any of them in the place of identity states the reversal. Apprehension can identify the rule. It cannot vote a different one into force.

exercises.prompt: Assemble the claim that consciousness takes the universe in and does not rule it.

feedback.note: Consciousness apprehends a universe it does not decree, because the three lines hold together: the universe is independent, awareness takes it in, and will is not its ruler. "Creates" would deny apprehension. "Chance" would add a ruler identity already excludes. The claim is the integration, not a new axiom beside existence and identity.

exercises.prompt: What is the law of causality, stated as a relation to identity?

choices.text: The law of identity applied to action
A second axiom that can override identity when things act
Constant conjunction, with no tie to what the entity is
A decree laid on things from outside their natures

feedback.note: Causality is the law of identity applied to action, because what a thing does follows from what it is. A second axiom that could override identity would let action break A is A. Constant conjunction is the Humean substitute, a sequence with no cause in the entity. A decree from outside the nature is a will set over identity. Causality is not a rival of identity.

exercises.prompt: Fire burns cotton and does not burn stone. Why do the two actions differ?

choices.text: Each action follows from what the cotton, the fire, and the stone are
The same sequence has been noticed, and the noticing is the cause
A will assigned burning to cotton for today and may reassign it
Cotton and stone share one nature, and the difference is unreal

feedback.note: Cotton burns and stone does not because those are different entities, and the action is caused by their natures. The noticing of a sequence is Humean constant conjunction, which leaves the natures out. A will that assigns burning is a decree. One shared nature would erase the difference identity requires. The cause is in the entities that act.

exercises.prompt: What does this passage establish about causality and identity?
exercises.quote: The law of causality is the law of identity applied to action.

choices.text: Causality is identity in the form of action, not a separate rule
Causality replaces identity whenever something acts
Action is exempt from identity
Causality is only the observation that one event follows another

feedback.quote: The law of causality is the law of identity applied to action.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 152
feedback.note: The passage identifies causality with identity applied to action, so it is not a second rule and it does not replace identity. Action is not exempt, because the application is to action. "One event follows another" is constant conjunction, and the passage does not say that. The law is one law, stated for action.

exercises.prompt: Someone treats causality as an extra law that could make a thing act against what it is. What has he done?

choices.text: He has split causality from identity and allowed the split to break A is A
He has stated what "applied to action" means
He has noticed that identity covers only things that are not acting
He has supplied the second law volition needs, because a mind has no nature

feedback.note: An extra law that can contradict identity is not identity applied to action, because a thing cannot act against its nature. "Applied to action" means the same law covers action, not that action gets an exemption. Identity is not limited to stillness. A mind has a nature too; volition is not a hole that a second law has to fill.

exercises.prompt: Match each name with the claim it makes about action.

pairs.right: A thing is what it is
That same fact, applied to what it does
A sequence with no cause in the entity

feedback.note: Identity says what the thing is, and causality applies that fact to action, because they are one law. Constant conjunction keeps the sequence and drops the entity's nature, which is the Humean error. A second axiom is the picture in which causality could break identity. That picture is the one this law rejects.

exercises.prompt: A critic says we only see that a spark comes before a flame, so the cause is our habit of expecting the flame. What has he left out?

choices.text: The natures of the spark and the fuel, which are what act
Nothing: expectation is the entity that burns
The Law of Identity, which he correctly treats as the habit
A divine will, which is the missing link in the sequence

feedback.note: The habit of expectation is Humean constant conjunction: one event, then another, with the cause placed in the observer. The spark and the fuel act as what they are, because the cause is their nature, not the expectation. Identity is not a habit. A divine will would be a decree, another substitute, not the missing piece of this law.

exercises.prompt: Complete the short statement of the law of causality.

feedback.note: Causality is identity applied to action, because the law says what the entity does, not a second fact beside what it is. Chance, a wish, or a vote would put an uncaused event, a feeling, or a tally in the place of the entity's nature. None of those is an application of identity. The word that keeps the law one law is action.

exercises.prompt: Assemble the short statement of causality.

feedback.note: Causality is identity applied to action, because the formula names one law rather than a rival. "Chance" or "decree" would replace the entity's nature with an uncaused event or a will. Either word states a substitute this law rejects. The order has to keep identity as what is applied, and action as what it is applied to.

exercises.prompt: Where is the cause of an action located?

choices.text: In the nature of the entities that act
In a push that has no entity behind it
In the observer's expectation that the action would occur
In a will that makes the entity act against its nature

feedback.note: The cause is the nature of the entities that act, because all actions are caused by entities. A push with nothing pushing erases the entity. Expectation is the Humean move, placing the cause in the observer. A will that drives a thing against its nature is a decree. None of those is a cause once the entity has been dropped or overruled.

exercises.prompt: Acid pits a metal, and a glass beaker holds the acid. What explains the two results?

choices.text: The natures of the acid, the metal, and the glass
A cause floating free of any of the three
The chemist's expectation that the metal would pit
A decree that could reverse the results with no change in the natures

feedback.note: The acid, the metal, and the glass act as what they are, so the pitting and the holding are their actions, because the cause is in those entities. A free-floating cause has no entity. The chemist's expectation does not pit metal. A decree that reversed the results without a change of nature would be action against identity, which causality does not permit.

exercises.prompt: What does this passage establish about the cause of an action?
exercises.quote: All actions are caused by entities.

choices.text: There is no action whose cause is not some entity
Actions cause themselves, and entities are optional
Only human choices are caused; other actions are not
Entities are caused by actions that float free of them

feedback.quote: All actions are caused by entities.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 151
feedback.note: The passage says all actions are caused by entities, so there is no remainder for a free-floating push, a chance event, or a decree, because the cause is some entity. Actions do not cause themselves. The "all" includes more than human choices. Reversing the order drops the thing that acts.

exercises.prompt: Someone says, "The cause is a force, and the entity is only where the force happens to sit." What is the error?

choices.text: The force is the action of entities, not a substitute that leaves them out
This is identity applied to action, correctly stated
A force with no nature is the primary existent
Constant conjunction is the entity he has identified

feedback.note: A force with no entity behind it is a push erased of the thing that acts, because actions are caused by entities and a force is their action. The remark does not state identity applied to action; it removes the identity. A nature-free force is not an existent of a specific kind. Constant conjunction is a sequence in observation, not the entity he claims to have found.

exercises.prompt: Match each item in the acid case with its role.

pairs.right: A cause with the entity erased
Not the cause of the pitting

feedback.note: The acid is an entity, and the pitting is what that entity does in contact with the metal, because the cause is their natures. A push with no thing behind it is the erased-entity error. Surprise is a state of the chemist, not a cause in the beaker. Expectation and decree are further substitutes, and neither is the acid.

exercises.prompt: Two balls strike and move. Someone says the cause is "the event of impact," and the balls' natures are scenery. What is wrong?

choices.text: The impact is the balls acting; dropping the balls drops the cause
Events cause events, and the entities are optional scenery
The cause is the player's wish that they move
The motion contradicts the balls' identity, which action is allowed to do

feedback.note: The impact is not a cause floating above the balls, because the balls are the entities that act and their natures set the motion. Event-beside-event is constant conjunction. The player's wish does not move the balls. Motion that fit the balls is not a contradiction of their identity. Removing the balls removes the only cause the law recognizes.

exercises.prompt: Complete the statement that locates the cause of an action.

feedback.note: Actions are caused by entities, because the nature of the thing that acts is the cause. Wishes, chances, and votes are the substitutes: a feeling, an uncaused event, and a tally. None of them acts in the place of the entity. A volitional consciousness is itself an entity, so a choice does not require a different kind of cause.

exercises.prompt: Assemble the claim about what determines an action.

feedback.note: The nature of the entities determines the action, because that is where the cause is located. "Chance" or "decree" would move the cause outside the entities, into an uncaused event or a will. The sentence stays true only while the entities' nature is the determiner. A push with no entity, and a habit of expectation, are the errors this wording excludes.

exercises.prompt: What does "a thing cannot act against its nature" rule out?

choices.text: An action that contradicts what the entity is
Every action, on the ground that identity means stillness
Change from one state to a later state
The choice to focus, on the ground that a mind has no nature

feedback.note: The clause rules out an action that contradicts the entity's nature, because causality is identity applied to action. It does not rule out action as such, and it does not rule out change over time. A mind has a nature: a volitional consciousness acts according to that nature when it focuses or does not. The choice is not the kind of breach the clause forbids.

exercises.prompt: A volitional consciousness either focuses or drifts. Why is that alternative not a break in causality?

choices.text: Focusing or not is the act of that kind of consciousness, so it acts as what it is
The alternative is uncaused chance
The alternative is a decree from outside the mind's nature
Causality pauses wherever a mind is in a position to choose

feedback.note: A volitional consciousness acts according to its nature when it chooses to focus or not, because the choice is an action under causality, not a hole in it. Chance would make the choice uncaused. A decree would place the cause outside the mind. A pause in causality would split the law of identity from action. The nature includes the alternative; it is not broken by it.

exercises.prompt: What does this passage establish about an action and the entity that acts?
exercises.quote: The nature of an action is caused and determined by the nature of the entities that act; a thing cannot act in contradiction to its nature.

choices.text: The entity's nature sets the action, and the entity cannot do the opposite of that
The action is set by a will outside the entity
Determination means the entity cannot act at all
An action that contradicts the entity's nature is a permitted kind of action

feedback.quote: The nature of an action is caused and determined by the nature of the entities that act; a thing cannot act in contradiction to its nature.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 152
feedback.note: The nature of an action is caused and determined by the nature of the entities that act, and a thing cannot act in contradiction to its nature. An outside will is a decree, not this cause. Determination does not mean stillness; it means the action fits what the entity is. A contradictory action is what the second clause rules out, not a permitted class.

exercises.prompt: Someone says, "If I can choose, the choice has no cause, so causality fails in the mind." What is the answer?

choices.text: The cause is the nature of a volitional consciousness; the choice is that nature in action
The choice shows that only sequences are real, as Hume held
A divine will has to fill the gap the choice opens
Identity does not apply to minds, so the failure is expected

feedback.note: The choice to focus or not is caused by the nature of the consciousness that chooses, so causality does not fail, because a volitional entity acts as what it is. Hume's sequences leave that nature out. A divine will would be a decree in the gap. Exempting minds from identity is the split this law rejects. Volition is not chance and not an exemption.

pairs.right: Action that fits what the stone is
The break that is not available

feedback.note: The stone falls as a stone, and it does not choose to hover, because a thing cannot act against its nature. A mind that focuses is acting as a volitional consciousness, which is its nature, not an exemption. Declaring the mind exempt would be the break causality does not contain. Change of position in the fall is not a contradiction.

exercises.prompt: Ice melts in heat. Someone demands that it stay solid because he needs it solid. What is the error in the demand?

choices.text: It asks the ice to act against the nature that sets its action
Melting is a contradiction inside the ice
Heat is only constant conjunction and not a cause
The need, if voted, becomes the ice's identity

feedback.note: The demand asks the ice to act against its nature, because the heat and the ice determine the melting. Melting is change, not a contradiction in the ice. Heat is a cause in the entities, not a bare sequence. A need or a vote does not become the ice's identity. That would be a decree, and causality does not permit it.

exercises.prompt: Complete the limit causality places on what a thing can do.

parts.text: A thing cannot act against its

feedback.note: A thing cannot act against its nature, because the action is determined by what the entity is. The past is not a rival of that nature; change over time is still action of the entity. Chance and a wish are the substitutes that would let an action float free of the entity. The limit is the nature, and action that fits the nature is still allowed.

exercises.prompt: Assemble the claim that focusing is an action under the mind's nature.

feedback.note: Focus acts by the mind's nature, because a volitional consciousness, in choosing to focus or not, acts as the kind of thing it is. "Against" would make the choice a contradiction of that nature. "Chance" would make it uncaused. Neither is causality. The choice is not a pause in the law, and it is not a decree from outside the mind.

exercises.prompt: Which list names substitutes that this account of causality rejects?

choices.text: Chance, a divine decree, and a second law that can break identity
The nature of the entity that acts
Identity applied to action
The fact that a volitional consciousness has a nature

feedback.note: Chance, decree, and a second law that could break identity are the substitutes, because causality is identity applied to the action of entities. The entity's nature is the cause, not a substitute for it. The volitional nature is a kind of entity, not a rival of the law. Rejecting the substitutes keeps one law rather than a cluster of exceptions.

exercises.prompt: Humean constant conjunction says we know only that one event follows another. What does that account leave out?

choices.text: The cause in the nature of the entities that act
The sequence, which this account denies ever happens
A freedom to ignore identity when the sequence is inconvenient
A decree, which the Humean account correctly retains

feedback.note: Constant conjunction keeps the "after" and drops the cause in the entities, because Hume's account has no necessary connection in their natures. This account does not deny that events are ordered; it says why the order is what it is. Inconvenience does not license a break in identity. Hume does not retain a decree; he retains a sequence. The missing piece is the entity.

exercises.prompt: What does this passage establish about the order of an effect and its conditions?
exercises.quote: The law of causality does not permit you to eat your cake before you have it.

choices.text: An effect cannot come before the conditions the entities make possible
You may have the effect first whenever a wish is strong enough
Causality is a second law that can grant the effect before the conditions
Chance may place the effect earlier than the cause

feedback.quote: The law of causality does not permit you to eat your cake before you have it.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 151
feedback.note: The passage says causality does not permit you to eat your cake before you have it, so the effect cannot precede the identity of the situation that makes it possible. A wish does not move the effect forward. A second law that granted the effect first would break identity. Chance is the same breach under another name. The order is set by what the entities are.

exercises.prompt: Someone says a god wills the cotton to burn, and the cotton's nature is irrelevant. What has replaced the cause?

choices.text: A decree has replaced the identity of the cotton
Nothing: this is identity applied to action
The decree is simply the nature of the cotton, under another name
Constant conjunction, which is the same thing as a decree

feedback.note: A will that burns the cotton while the cotton's nature is irrelevant is a divine decree, because the cause has been moved outside the entity. That is not identity applied to action. The decree is not another name for the cotton's nature; it is a denial that the nature matters. Constant conjunction is a different substitute, a bare sequence, not the same claim as this will.

exercises.prompt: Match each account of why something happened with the view it is.

pairs.left: The cause is the entity's nature
One event after another, and nothing more
A will sets the action from outside

feedback.note: Only the entity's nature is the cause this law recognizes, because action is identity in act. Constant conjunction stops at the sequence. Chance denies a cause. A divine decree puts a will outside the nature. These are not three wordings of one theory. They are the rivals, and each drops or overrules the entity.

exercises.prompt: Someone says causality is an extra axiom, so a miracle may break identity and leave causality standing. What is the error?

choices.text: There is no room for the break: causality is identity in action, and the miracle would deny both
A miracle is only change over time, so identity allows it
Identity covers thoughts and causality covers bodies, so they may split
A vote can authorize the exception without touching either law

feedback.note: A miracle that broke identity would break causality with it, because they are one law and not an axiom plus an extra. Change over time is an entity acting as what it is, not a suspension of what it is. Splitting minds and bodies invents two laws. A vote cannot authorize a contradiction in nature. The exception is the rival picture, not a clause of the law.

exercises.prompt: Complete the relation of causality to identity.

parts.text: Causality is not a second law beside

feedback.note: Causality is not a second law beside identity, because it is identity applied to action. Chance, decree, and conjunction are the rivals one might try to set beside it, and each is a different error. The law must stay attached to identity. Detaching it is what lets a miracle, a will, or a bare sequence pretend to be a cause.

exercises.prompt: Assemble the rejection of the two most common substitute causes.

feedback.note: Causality is not chance and not a decree, because an uncaused event and an outside will both drop the entity's nature. "Habit" would name the Humean expectation, and "wish" would name a feeling; both are further substitutes, not the claim. The law stays identity applied to action. Volition does not join the list of substitutes, because a choosing mind acts as what it is.

exercises.prompt: How do the short formula and the longer clause stand to each other?

choices.text: As one statement: identity in action means the nature sets the act and bars its opposite
As two laws that are allowed to conflict
The short formula forbids action, and the longer clause restores it
The longer clause replaces identity with constant conjunction

feedback.note: The short formula, identity applied to action, and the longer clause, that the entities' nature determines the action and cannot be contradicted, are one statement, because the clause spells out the formula. Two conflicting laws would split them. The formula does not forbid action. The clause does not smuggle in a bare sequence. The fuller wording is the same law.

exercises.prompt: A spark, oxygen, and dry timber produce a fire. What do the short formula and the longer clause both say?

choices.text: The fire is those entities acting as what they are, and the timber cannot burn as if it were stone
The fire is chance, which identity does not cover
The fire is a decree, and the entities are passive occasions
The fire may precede the timber when someone needs the effect first

feedback.note: Both wordings say the fire is the action of those entities according to their natures, and that the timber cannot act as a different kind of thing, because that is one law. Chance drops the natures. A decree makes them passive. An effect before the timber would be eating the cake first. The fuller statement does not add a cause the short formula left out.

exercises.prompt: Someone accepts "identity applied to action" but denies that the entity's nature determines the action. What has he done?

choices.text: He has cut the formula off from the clause that states its meaning
He has stated the full law in both of its wordings
He has adopted the Humean account under the name of the formula
He has separated a man-made rule from a given fact that need not agree with it

feedback.note: Denying the determining role of the nature empties the formula, because "applied to action" means precisely that the nature sets the action. He has not stated the full law. The Humean account is the rival he has approached, a sequence with the nature left out, and it is not a reading of the formula. The two wordings are not a man-made rule versus a given fact; they are one statement.

exercises.prompt: Someone treats the longer clause as permission to add chance beside identity, as a minor cause. What is wrong?

choices.text: The longer clause is the same law, and chance is not a minor cause inside it
A fuller wording is allowed to break the axiom it applies
Chance is the nature of every entity, so the addition is harmless
The longer clause is a vote about how the short formula should be read

feedback.note: Chance is not a minor partner of identity, because the longer clause says the nature determines the action and a thing cannot act against that nature. A fuller wording that broke identity would not be a fuller statement of the law. Chance is not a nature. A vote does not adjudicate between the two wordings. They stand or fall together.

exercises.prompt: Match each wording with the job it does in the one law.

pairs.left: The entity's nature determines the action
A rival law that can suspend identity
